timeline: You might assume a falling drill bit only ruins a tool, but how did it swallow an entire lake on November 20, 1980?

A fourteen-inch drill bit pierced an inactive level of the salt mine.
Water rushed down into deep subterranean caverns.
Fifty-five miners fled safely up the mine's elevator shaft.
An oil rig and eleven barges vanished downward.
The reverse flow created a giant temporary waterfall.
Remarkably, zero human lives were lost that day.
Days later, nine sunken barges popped back up.
